\section{Notation and typed identities}
\label{sec:notation}

This module fixes the symbols used by both views of the SCI-AST v0.1
authority.  A symbol is meaningful only together with its declared identity,
unit, frame, topology, support, parent, validity, and availability.  Array
position or a similar name is never an identity.

\subsection{Indices and scientific objects}

\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.16\linewidth}
                  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.76\linewidth}}
\toprule
Symbol & Meaning \\
\midrule
\endhead
$o$ & Immutable observation identity. \\
$d$ & Admitted detector/acquisition occurrence, including its observation
binding; it is not merely an array row or an optional design identity. \\
$s$ & Stable detector-reference slot identity on the exact admitted SCI-ALIGN
grid.  Its stable identity is $(o,s)$; it is independent of any local storage
row or numerical array position. \\
$j$ & Local storage row only.  It is never an external identity, an ALIGN
slot, an occurrence identity, or a scientific parent. \\
$n$ & Stable output-sample identity on an exact resolved SCI-RTC output grid. \\
$k\in\{0,1\}$ & Producer-selected pointing-support record identity. \\
$p$ & Pixel identity used by a MAP-owned deposition/gridding operator. \\
$F$ & Declared output frame.  $H$ denotes the declared native horizon frame;
$J$ denotes the explicitly identified equatorial J2000 frame used by Science.
The letters do not supply missing frame semantics. \\
$\widehat{\boldsymbol u}_{\rm sky}$ & Unit sky direction in a declared
spherical frame.  Symbols $x$ and $r$ are reserved exclusively for the paired
KID readout coordinates. \\
$\boldsymbol e_\ell,\boldsymbol e_b$ & Local orthonormal tangent basis toward
increasing longitude at fixed latitude and increasing latitude. \\
$\boldsymbol c_k,\boldsymbol c_s$ & Pointing-support correction and its
realization at stable ALIGN slot $s$, expressed as declared tangent
components in radians. \\
$\boldsymbol g_d$ & Selected detector-geometry datum, including its immutable
APT realization and occurrence binding. \\
$\mathcal G_\gamma$ & Selected, versioned geometry and field-rotation relation
with lineage $\gamma$; it includes the declared gauge, basis, handedness,
pivot state, affine limitations, time/elevation support, and uncertainty
availability. \\
$\boldsymbol\xi_{ds}$ & Realized detector tangent displacement supplied by
$\mathcal G_\gamma$ at the current aligned sample time and elevation. \\
$\mathsf R_{F\leftarrow H,s}$ & Named frame operator from the declared native
horizon frame to $F$ at stable slot $s$, including required time, site,
epoch/equinox, EOP/refraction policy, version, and validity. \\
$\boldsymbol w$ & Continuous tangent-plane coordinate, in arcseconds for
Point/OOF/Beammap and degrees for Science. \\
$\boldsymbol q=(q_1,q_2)^\mathsf T$ & Continuous one-based FITS pixel
coordinate. \\
$(j,h)$ & Zero-based local storage row and column.  Neither is an external
identity; $j$ is reserved for local storage row only. \\
$\mathcal W_o$ & Immutable realized WCS identity for the declared
observation/product plan. \\
$\theta^A_{ds}$ & AST coordinate on the exact ALIGN-grid parent. \\
$\theta^{\rm RTC}_{dn}$ & Separately parented AST coordinate on the exact
resolved RTC output grid with stable role
\texttt{SCI-AST:rtc\_output\_grid\_coordinates@1}. \\
$G_{pi}$ & Estimator-specific sample-to-pixel deposition/gridding operator
owned by SCI-MAP, even when materialized by AST as a delegated service. \\
$\mathcal B^{\rm AST}_i$ & Base pre-MAP AST facts: continuous FITS pixel,
optional nominal containing pixel under its declared rule, and bounds state;
never a kernel-dependent neighborhood or estimator support. \\
$J_{\rm AST,0}^{({\rm out}\leftarrow{\rm in})}$ & Typed
\texttt{astrometric\_map\_center\_jacobian}, evaluated at the declared
physical center. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\subsection{Units, topology, and indexing}

Angles used by the spherical equations are radians unless an equation states
otherwise.  Define
\begin{equation}
  \kappa \equiv \frac{\pi}{180\,3600}
  \quad\text{radian per arcsecond}.
  \label{eq:kappa}
\end{equation}
FITS/WCS pixel coordinates are one-based.  In-memory rows and columns are
zero-based.  Internal windows and supports are half-open and retain stable
identities.  A longitude component must declare whether it is a coordinate
increment or an on-sky tangent component.

For a period $P$, \emph{shortest signed difference} means a deterministic
member of $[-P/2,P/2)$, while persisted normalized longitude is a member of
$[0,P)$.  Exactly antipodal interpolation is unavailable unless an explicit
unwrap authority selects the path and parents that selection.  At a
coordinate pole, the unit vector rather than longitude is the direction
identity.

\subsection{Exact parent identities}

The parent of an ALIGN-grid detector sky direction is
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \Pi^{A,{\rm direction}}_{ds}=(o,d,s,\;&
  \text{SCI-ALIGN\_TO\_SCI-AST v0.1/r0.1},\\
  &\text{ALIGN plan/grid/source relation},\;\text{observing state},\\
  &\text{pointing correction},\;\gamma,\;F).
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:align-parent}
\end{equation}
It binds the stable slot $(o,s)$ and never a local row $j$.  The exact ALIGN
profile is compatible only when its profile identity and declared
version/revision preserve every required identity, semantic state, ownership
boundary, and typed-availability rule.  A successor must name the revision it
supersedes and map every changed, removed, or newly required item explicitly;
similar shape or field names do not establish compatibility.

The successive tangent, continuous-pixel, and nominal-pixel roles add only
their scientific dependencies:
\begin{align}
 \Pi^{A,{\rm tangent}}_{ds}
   &= (\Pi^{A,{\rm direction}}_{ds},\;
       \text{selected physical center},\;
       \text{tangent projection identity}),
       \label{eq:tangent-parent}\\
 \Pi^{A,{\rm pixel}}_{ds}
   &= (\Pi^{A,{\rm tangent}}_{ds},\;\mathcal W_o),
       \label{eq:pixel-parent}\\
 \Pi^{A,{\rm nominal\ pixel}}_{ds}
   &= (\Pi^{A,{\rm pixel}}_{ds},\;\text{rounding rule},\;
       \text{dimensions},\;\text{bounds convention}).
       \label{eq:nominal-pixel-parent}
\end{align}
Consequently a WCS failure cannot erase a valid direction or tangent fact,
and a nominal-pixel failure cannot erase a valid continuous pixel.  A
requested product family may still require atomic completion and fail that
product while preserving the individual facts and exact causes.

The parent of $\theta^{\rm RTC}_{dn}$ extends the appropriate available
direction, tangent, or pixel role rather than relabeling it:
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \Pi^{\rm RTC}_{dn} = (o,d,n,\;&\Pi^{A,{\rm role}}_{dM_n},
   \text{SCI-AST:rtc\_output\_grid\_coordinates@1},\\
   &\text{RTC product/plan/grid},M_n,t_n,\\
   &\text{phase/delay/time shift},\text{segment},\text{decimation},\\
   &\text{full support/temporal response/correction state}).
 \end{aligned}
 \label{eq:rtc-parent}
\end{equation}
Here $M_n$ denotes the exact RTC-selected representative stable ALIGN slot
when applicable; it is never selected by AST.  The selected role and every
response/correction fact are part of the identity.

\subsection{Availability and cause types}

Every optional or unresolved quantity carries a typed state and exact reason.
The vocabulary used here is:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \texttt{available} and \texttt{available\_conditional};
  \item \texttt{unavailable\_input}, \texttt{unavailable\_authority}, and
        \texttt{unavailable\_unsupported}; and
  \item \texttt{not\_applicable} and \texttt{not\_persisted\_standard}.
\end{itemize}
A producer may refine these states, but must not collapse unavailable into
numeric zero or an empty unlabeled field.

Five cause types are distinct throughout:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.]
  \item detector-occurrence identity;
  \item detector signal-coordinate validity and numerical payload
        availability for $x$ and $r$;
  \item SCI-ALIGN mapping validity;
  \item SCI-AST coordinate validity; and
  \item downstream use-specific eligibility under a named owner's policy.
\end{enumerate}
No cause is an alias, precedence rule, or rescue rule for another.
